surprises.head: Colorado kept finding open men against Devin Cooley
surprises.body: Cooley allowed 7 goals on 30 shots, worth 2.9 expected goals: 4.1 more than expected, though five of them came off a pass that set up the shooter. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 200 starts. Most starters don’t get one a season.

story.head: The Avalanche roll past the Flames
paras: T.J. Hughes picked up his first NHL point. Devon Toews opened the scoring for the Avalanche late in the first, but Adam Klapka tied it 1-1 for Calgary less than two minutes later. Toews, Cale Makar and Nathan MacKinnon scored three goals in just under five minutes early in the second to put the Avalanche up 4-1. Zachary L'Heureux and Matt Coronato squared off midway through the period. There were five goals in the third period alone. Cale Makar and Jaden Schwartz scored 59 seconds apart early in the period to stretch the lead to 6-1. Mikael Backlund and Kevin Bahl scored a little over a minute apart later in the period to cut Colorado’s lead to 6-3. Schwartz scored his second of the night a little over a minute later to make it 7-3 for the Avalanche. The Flames’ Jonathan Castagna played his first NHL game and picked up a point. Two players had three-point nights: MacKinnon with a goal and two assists, and Cale Makar with two goals and an assist.

Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Scott Wedgewood made 26 saves for the Avalanche, and Devin Cooley allowed seven goals on 30 shots. The Avs moved to 3-1-0, climbing to second in the Central. The Flames fell to 0-4-0, still last in the NHL.

items.text: The Flames are 0-4-0, still looking for their first win.
The Avalanche have beaten the Flames four straight times, going back to last season.
All three of the preview’s calls held.
